title.narrative: Human Rights, Inclusion and Empowerment Trust Fund 2020-2022 (2025)
Human Rights, Inclusion and Empowerment Trust Fund 2020-2022 (2025)

description.narrative:
Fonden för mänskliga rättigheter, inkludering och Empowerment (Human Rights, Inclusion and Empowerment Fund) – HRIETF är en fond inom Världsbanken (VB) vars verksamhet bygger på erfarenheter och lärdomar (utvärdering gjord 2017) från den tidigare Nordic Trust Fund (NTF).
HRIETF har ett WBG (World Bank Group)-mandat och dess övergripande mål är att "öka och stärka förståelsen och tillämpningen av principerna för mänskliga rättigheter i WBG´s arbete". Genom tekniskt och finansiellt stöd vill HRIETF öka den interna kunskapen om mänskliga rättigheter och hur mänskliga rättigheter kan integreras i Världsbankens verksamhet. För att uppnå detta avser HRIETF att arbeta strategiskt med WBG ledarskap/chefskap för att säkerställa att mänskliga rättigheter inkluderas och integreras på institutionell nivå i organisationen. Dess syfte är även att ge finansiellt bidrag till VBs landskontor och tematiska enheter på huvudkontoret för att integrera mänskliga rättigheter i sin verksamhet. Fonden kommer också att fokusera sitt arbete på kommunikation, kunskapshantering, lärande och partnerskapsbyggande. HRIETF kommer arbeta genom sex tematiska fönster för att nå sitt övergripande mål; 1)Demokrati, Institutioner och Empowerment, 2) Infrastruktur, 3) ) Sårbarhet, Konflikt, Våld och Tvångsförflyttning, 4) Forskning och Utvärdering) och 5) Social Inkludering samt 6) Programhantering och Administration.
HRIETF är ett ”kunskaps- och lärande” initiativ som inrättades 2009 av Danmark, Finland, Island, Norge och Sverige och senare anslöt sig även Tyskland. Fonden har haft sin organisatoriska hemvist på olika enheter inom VB genom åren. I oktober 2019 påbörjade ett organisatoriskt förändringsarbete inom banken vilket i förlängningen kom att innebära att fonden flyttats från Governance avdelningen till avdelningen för Social Utveckling.
NTF´s övergripande mål var att hjälpa banken att ”utveckla en ökad uppfattning om hur de mänskliga rättigheterna förhåller sig till organisationens analytiska och operativa verksamhet”. Dess verksamhet var att utforska och identifiera innovativa metoder för att integrera rättighetsperspektivet i organisationen för att nå VB-målet att minska fattigdomen och öka det gemensamma välståndet. NTF gav ekonomiskt bidrag till VBs landkontor samt enheter på huvudkontoret och bidrog med tekniskt stöd till Världsbanks team för att utforska sambandet mellan deras arbete och mänskliga rättigheter. Sedan 2010 har fonden godkänt 111 bidrag i fem bidrags-rundor, genomsnitt US $240 000 och med ett maximalt beviljande av US $450 000.
I denna nya fas har HRIETF, vidareutvecklat tre strategier som fokuserar på kommunikation, kunskapshantering, lärande och partnerskap. Kommunikationsstrategin är inriktad mot identifiering av viktiga målgrupper och partners med syfte att på ett strategiskt vis kommunicera verksamheten samt dess resultat. Den övergripande målsättningen för kunskapshantering och lärande är att öka tillämpningen av mänskliga rättigheter i och utanför projektbidragen och därigenom bidra till att lärandet institutionaliseras. Den tredje strategin är partnerskapsstrategin som omfattar partnerskap mellan både externa och interna partners.
The Nordic Trust Fund (NTF), har nu bytt namn till HRIETF utvärderades 2017 (2009 - 2017). Sammanfattningsvis har NTF bidragit till att minska vissa av spänningarna som relaterar till mänskliga rättigheter inom VB. VB-team har integrerat mänskliga rättighet i sitt arbete på ett sätt som har upplevts som stärkande. De ekonomiska bidragen (grants) har bidragit till att bygga kunskap bland VB-team när det gäller att genomföra projekt och påverka attityder och beteenden i relation till mänskliga rättigheter. Projekt har lett till institutionell förändring inom VB, till exempel antagandet av strategin för sexuell orientering och könsidentitet samt både antagande och implementering av ramverket för miljö och socialfrågor som uttryckligen hänvisar till mänskliga rättigheter.
Sidas erfarenhet av att samarbeta med fonden har varit positiv. Dialogen med sekretariatet och andra givare har varit produktiv och robust. Resultaten av kontinuerlig och tät diskussion speglas i det nya och förstärkta projektdokument där resultatstyrning förstärkts och strategin för projekt (grants) har omarbetats och är nu mer systematisk och strategisk. Det kvarstår utmaningar som reflekteras i de identifierade dialogfrågorna samt i riskerna. Dialogfrågor kommer Sida att driva i dialog med banken, fondens sekretariat och andra givare under avtalsperioden.
VB har genom olika initativ svarat mot covid -19 pandemin. Fonden för diskussioner internt om hur man på bästa sätt ska involvera fondens aktiviteter i responsen. I det nästkommande PC (sept. 2020) kommer frågan att diskutteras i mer detalj.

The World Bank Group (WBG) through the Human Rights, Inclusion and Empowerment Trust Fund (HRIETF ) is mandated and committed (through its five institutions) to reduce poverty and increase shared prosperity (Twin-goals). The HRIETF follows on from the Nordic Trust Fund (NTF) and is based on discussions with the NTF donors during the second quarter 2019. The HRIETF is placed within the WBG at the Social Development Practice. The HRIETF has a WBG mandate, and the development objective of the TF is: “increase and strengthen the understanding and application of human rights principles in the WBG´s work”. Through technical and financial support, the HRIETF want to scale up internal capacity on human rights. It aims to work strategically with the WBG management to ensure institutional advancement of human rights in its operations. In addition, the HRIETF will provide grants to WB teams (WBG Country Management Units at country level and to WBG practices at the headquarters) to integrate human rights into its operations. It will also scale- its communication and knowledge management & learning work. The HRIETF has sexthematic windows in which it aims to operate; 1) Governance, Inclusive Institutions and Empowerment, 2) Infrastructure, 3) Fragility, Conflict, Violence and Forced Displacement, 4) Research and Evaluation, 5) Social Inclusion and 6) Program management and Administration.The HRIETF is a knowledge and learning initiative established in 2009 by Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden, and joined later by Germany. The mandate of the NTF was to help the Bank develop an informed view of how human rights relate to its analytical and operational activities. Its objectives were to explore and identify innovative approaches for incorporating human rights perspectives and empowering vulnerable groups to help make WBG analysis and operations more effective in reducing poverty and boosting shared prosperity. It did so through a grant program that provided financial and technical support to World Bank teams interested in exploring the link between their work and human rights. Since 2010 the grant program has approved 111 grants in five grant rounds, averaging US$ 240,000 and with a maximum grant of US$ 450,000.In addition to the programme document, the Secretariat has developed three strategies that focuses on Communication, Knowledge Management and Learning and Partnerships. The communication strategy is centered on identification of key audiences and partners for communicating results. The Knowledge Management and Learning strategy overall goal is to increase the uptake of human rights in and beyond the grants, thereby contributing to learning being captured and institutionalized. The third strategy is the partnership strategy which encompasses Trust Fund wider partnerships.In 2017 the Nordic Trust Fund (NTF), now HRIETF (name change in 2020) was evaluated (2009 - 2017). In sum, the NTF has contributed to alleviating some of the tensions with respect to human rights issues within the WBG. Sida´s experience engaging with the TF has been positive. The dialogue with the secretariat and other donors have been productive and robust. The results of these discussion can be mirrored in the new and strengthened project document where results based managed has been reinforced and the strategy for grant making has been modified and is now more systematic and strategic. Several challenges however remain; the TF ability to demonstrate results on impact level is one such example. The identified dialogue issues will be important to explicitly emphasize in the upcoming agreement period.Covid -19 has had severe impact on our whole society. The World Bank Group has put in place a response. The role of the TF in this response is not clear. It is however something Sida aims to follow closely in dialogue with the Secretariat but also to raise in the upcoming PC.

Objectives and outcomes of the intervention The main objective of the HRIETF is to "increase and strengthen the understanding and application of human rights principles in the WBG work". Through technical and financial support, the HRIETF aims to scale up internal capacity of human rights in the WBG through the HRIETF-supported activities. The TF has the following outcomes: Outcome 1: Human Rights are incorporated into analytical products and operations Outcome 2: WB staff and management understand and value the incorporation of human rights in development Outcome 3: Partnerships influence analysis and/or operations supported by the HRIETF The above results will be achieved through sex thematic funding windows; Governance, Inclusive Institutions and Empowerment, 2) Infrastructure, 3) Fragility, Conflict, Violence and Forced Displacement, 4) Research and Evaluation, 5) Social Inclusion and 6) Program management and Administration.

title.narrative: Beslut om insats, VB Human Rights, Inclusion and Empowerment Trust Fund 2020-2022

description.narrative:
The Word Bank Human Rights, Inclusion and Empowerment Trust Fund, HRIE provides technical and financial support to World Bank Group staff interested in applying human rights standards, methodology, principles, and approaches in operational and analytical work. In addition to supporting ongoing grants and a new call for proposals, HRIE continued to foster internal and external partnerships during the reporting period.
The Grant Program
From January 2022 through June 2023, HRIE TF implemented 48 grants that addressed a broad array of human rights issues, including racism in the Middle East and North Africa, the rights of women with disabilities globally, the role of transport in promoting human rights in Bangladesh, and LGBTI rights in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. One overarching focus of HRIE during the reporting period has been to increase the WBs engagement in inclusion of marginalized individuals and groups and those at risk of discrimination or disadvantage in their country or region. The grant program worked to advance human rights in three key ways during the reporting period: i) Generating Data to advance to Understand Gaps in Human Rights ii) Fostering Engagement with, and Training of, Rights Holders and Duty Bearers and iii) Informing Policy Reform to Promote Human Rights.
Examples
Solid understanding of the specific needs of populations at risk, and in many cases of the determinants of discrimination, is critical to designing and implementing effective programs and policies to reach the most marginalized groups. The Fund expresses it has played an important role at the Bank in fostering data collection and research regarding some of those groups, including funding the earliest research on disability and development and on the costs of discrimination against LGBTQ individuals. Some highlights expressed in the report for the period 2022 and 2023 included:
-Research exploring implications of the use of new technologies on human rights. A grant focusing on "human rights and cybersecurity financed research for a report, Cybersecurity and Human Rights (World Bank 2023), that addresses human rights in the digital world. It discusses a model for building an information environment that reduces the impact of disinformation and other social harm without resorting to censorship or other infringements on human rights. The report helps development practitioners ensure that project design for digital infrastructure mitigates potential human rights impacts. Similarly, the grant Anticorruption and Human Rights has analyzed the overlaps between the human rights and anticorruption agendas. By systematizing documents produced by the United Nations Human Rights Council as part of the Universal Periodic Review mechanism, this grant exemplifies how World Bank staff can make better use of human rights global institutions for dialogue on anticorruption, and vice versa." (Page 15.)
-Empirical analyses of human trafficking. "In collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the team conducted an empirical analysis using unique micro-level trafficked victims database compiled and updated by IOM. The work demonstrated the relationship between economic shocks and human trafficking and highlighted the role of factors such as good governance, commitment to the rule of law and access to justice, and strict antitrafficking policies. The grants work stressed the need to frame policy responses to human trafficking under states broad legal obligation from a human rights point of view. These findings are particularly relevant because they highlight how economic shocks, particularly those induced by events like the COVID19 pandemic and the current conflict in Ukraine will impact patterns of human trafficking. The report on this project was published in 2022 (World Bank and IOM 2022)." (Page 15.)
-Under the "Fostering Engagement with, and Training of, Rights Holders and Duty Bearers" area of the Grant Program, the grant "Gina Mata, Gina AlUmma: Build Up Women, Build the Community funded the design and introduction of a pilot program to support digital skills development and human rights training for disadvantaged young women and girls in Kano, Nigeria. The grant is designed to break their cycle of unemployment and vulnerability to genderbased violence. The program was implemented in the states of Kano (200 participants) and Jigawa (155 participants) and will be extended to three more states." (Page 16.)
-Under the area "Informing Policy Reform to Promote Better Realization of Human Rights" of the Grant Program, the funding provided enhanced efforts to inform country-level policy reform in several human rights issues such as:
-The grant Supporting Indigenous Peoples Efforts to Identify, Secure, and Enforce Communities Land Tenure Rights in DRC influenced the design of the governments policy on land tenure to include the Indigenous peoples agenda. - The grant on Embedding the rights of women with disabilities in World Bank operations has, according to the report, generated critical data on legal frameworks to inform policy engagement globally by assessing gender and disability laws and policies worldwide. "Drawing on the methodology of the World Banks Women, Business, and the Law initiative, this grant supported ground-breaking data collection and preparation of several policy briefs on the design of gender- and disabilityinclusive laws and policies. Based on the data and interviews with World Bank task teams, the team produced a toolkit on including women and girls with disabilities in World Bank operations, which provides examples from team leaders who have led successful gender and disability-inclusive operations and lists World Bank Group commitments to women with disabilities, key barriers and solutions in several sectors, and a checklist for project teams." (Report page 16)
-The 2022 grant-funded report Integrating Gender Considerations into Public Transport Policies and Operations identified best practices for genderresponsive infrastructure policies, and provided key insights that World Bank staff, governments, and other stakeholders can use to enhance womens and girls human rights.
Strategic Priorities for the Grant Program
In addition to the above key impact areas, the Grant Program has four strategic priorities: Infrastructure Governance Fragility Violence and Conflict and Social Inclusion.
Infrastructure Grants examples during the reporting period
"The World Bank helps developing countries build infrastructure that can support inclusive, sustainable growth. Access to adequate infrastructure is necessary for the realization of several human rights, allowing people not only to access their jobs and other activities, but also to participate actively in society and engage in activities that enable them to realize their socioeconomic, civil, political, and cultural human rights. During 2022, the HRIE TF funded grants that applied innovative approaches to the design of infrastructure that affect populations at greater risk of discrimination or exclusion, particularly children, women, and people with disabilities." (Page 18.)
The report provide several examples under this section, for instance: "The grant Tools for Identifying Human Rights Impact and Ensuring Algorithmic Accountability in World Bank Operations Using Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics was designed to develop a guidance tool to ensure adoption of a human rights-based approach regarding artificial intelligence (AI) in Bank operations. This project is designed to build bridges between the theoretical aspects of human rights and the practical implications of AI and emerging technologies as they are related to development initiatives across sectors such as health care and social protection. Although designed to raise awareness of World Bank staff to enable trustworthy and accountable use of AI in connection with achieving the World Banks goals of ensuring sustainable, resilient, inclusive development, it is hoped that the initiative will also inform and inspire other development partners, organizations, and stakeholders. This innovative grant will help World Bank staff identify when AI components might affect human rights and how algorithmic accountability could mitigate those risks." (Page 19.)
Governance, Inclusive Institutions, and Empowerment Grants
Grants under this strategic priority "help identify structural causes of corruption, poor governance, discrimination, and exclusion". In 2022, there were several grants focusing on reinforcing states efforts to design public policies that enhance access to human rights. For instance, the grant "Strengthening implementation of Sustainable Development Goals 10 and 17 for Disability Inclusion in Nigeria provided technical support to the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities, which with the support of the World Bank team, identified strategic approaches to disabilityinclusive development and established the National Partnership for DisabilityInclusive Development, which brings together various organizations, including from the private sector, to work toward disability inclusion in Nigeria. The guidelines developed focus on topics such as monitoring and compliance, gender and child protection, stakeholder communication, discrimination, and disability inclusion in employment." (Page 19.)
Another interesting result is the grant "Supporting the Realization of Access Rights in Latin America and the Caribbean through the Escazú Agreement objective has been to support the realization of access rights that the Escazú Agreement recognizes by identifying implementation, awarenessraising, and capacity-building opportunities in selected countries and developing a methodological framework to integrate its provisions into the Banks operational and analytical work. To do so, the team has formed a partnership with the United Nations Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean, which is the Secretariat for the agreement. A first diagnostic report identified gaps, challenges, and opportunities to implement the Escazú Agreement. This report has informed the efforts of the government of Argentina to comply with the Escazú treaty. The team has an ongoing engagement with Colombia on participation rights and is in advanced discussions with Belize to support an Escazú implementation roadmap." (Page 20.) It is noted that the" activities and lessons that this grant identified will help the World Bank and other international financial institutions identify best practices to support countries as they prepare to implement the provisions of the Escazú Agreement and, in so doing, support realization of environmental human rights and inclusive decision making." (Page 20.)
Social Inclusion Grants
Grants under this strategic priority focus on "inclusion of LGTBI people and persons with disabilities and activities to foster the rights of Indigenous peoples and ethnic minorities." Six new grants received support from the Fund in 2022, for instance the grant Understanding and Building Indigenous Peoples Resilience to Climate Shocks, which is designed to "identify key drivers and legal and institutional enablers that support Indigenous peoples resilience to climate and other external shocks". (Page 20.) Fieldwork was conducted that "documented successful strategies that indigenous peoples in 10 countries across three regions (Africa, Latin America, South Asia) use. The results of the fieldwork have informed a draft framework for indigenous peoples resilience, including a definition and identification of endogenous drivers and external enablers, as well as a set of indicators. The draft framework is being shared for discussion and participatory refinement and validation in three regional roundtables and one global dialogue with indigenous thought leaders, government partners, and representatives from each case study. The roundtables are being organized in conjunction with other key regional policy meetings such as the African Climate Summit, the Latin America and Caribbean Climate Week, the International Conference on Indigenous Research and Education, and the 28th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change Change to support indigenous peoples participation in these events and articulation of priorities and proposals. The knowledge that this work generates will not only inform World Bank financing and investments on risks and ways to support Indigenous peoples resilience, but will also serve as a global public good, adding to understanding of and evidence on issues most critical for indigenous peoples, such as capacity to adapt to a changing climate." (Page 20.)
"The impact of this grant on indigenous peoples visibility and attention was made evident during the recent African Climate Summit indigenous peoples were invited to share their proposals and concerns during the opening and closing ceremonies of this regional event that thousands of people attended, including heads of state, ministers, and other highlevel representatives from the global development community. This grants activities have also received attention from other partnerships across the Bank, such as EnABLE and ProGreen, demonstrating its capacity to increase inclusion of indigenous peoples rights in Bank activities." (Page 20.)
In addition, the grant "Disability Inclusion and Rights Data Hub aims to collect disability-disaggregated data and indicators for multiple stakeholders. The grant also seeks to produce a data hub that is accessible to persons with different disabilities. "By providing highquality, policyrelevant data and disability-disaggregated development indicators, this project will fill an important gap that will benefit World Bank Group staff, governments, and other stakeholders and allow states efforts to adhere to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities to be tracked." (Page 20.)
Fragility, Conflict, Violence, and Forced Displacement Grants
Human rights violations and conflict are intricately connected. Violent conflict erodes individuals wellbeing and violates their human rights, and lack of respect for human rights is one of the key drivers of violent conflict. According to the report, the fund's grants are innovative and designed to uncover opportunities to support and enhance the lives of individuals and groups harmed by conflict. Some examples in 2022: "Three grants Technical Assistance for the Implementation of the Integral Plan for the Attention and Protection of Venezuelan Population in Conditions of Human Mobility in Ecuador Addressing Human Rights Gaps among Venezuelan Migrants due to Gender in Colombia and Perú and Venezuelan Migration Policy Dialogue and Technical Assistance in Colombia provided technical assistance to countries hosting many refugees and internally displaced populations to create policies that guarantee displaced persons human rights and help with their integration into host communities. These grants provide technical assistance to host governments to guarantee human rights and promote migrants selfreliance and economic participation, which supports governments and helps capitalize on potential benefits from this migration in the medium term. It also informs policies and government actions to promote social integration, including mitigation of xenophobia and discrimination against migrants in the host society, which are critical for ensuring that migrants human rights are respected." (Page 22.)
In 2022, "activities funded by a grant on human trafficking produced a comprehensive empirical analysis of the impact of economic shocks on human trafficking and identified lessons on the institutions that can help moderate the effects of economic shocks on people who have been trafficked. Two documents were published: the policy brief Economic Shocks and Human Trafficking Risks: Evidence from IOMs Victims of Human Trafficking Database, produced by HRIE and the IOM, and the report Economic Shocks and Human Trafficking Risks, published by the World Bank and the IOM." (Page 22.)
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
